grade.rationale: The implementation is compact and generally robust, but evidence attribution is insufficiently validated and path matching can silently omit applicable findings. Duplicate sensor configurations are also discarded without detecting conflicts.

observations.summary: The collector handles cancellation and sensor failures cleanly and produces consistently ordered results. The main risks are accepting misleading provenance, incomplete path normalization during subject projection, and silently choosing one of multiple configurations for the same sensor.

findings.title: Returned provenance is not verified against the invoked sensor
findings.description: The validation only requires each finding to claim a deterministic source with a nonblank sensor ID. It does not require Finding.Source.SensorId or result.Provenance.SensorId to equal sensor.Id, nor verify that the result provenance is deterministic and internally consistent. A faulty sensor can therefore attribute findings or the entire result to another sensor, after which ordering and prompt projection propagate the misleading identity.
findings.recommendation: Validate that result.Provenance.SensorId and every finding Source.SensorId equal sensor.Id using the registry's intended ID comparison semantics. Also validate any other required provenance invariants before accepting the result, and convert violations into an unavailable result as currently done.

findings.title: Equivalent repository paths can fail subject matching
findings.description: NormalizePath only changes separator characters and removes leading "./" segments. It does not collapse interior dot segments, repeated separators, or parent segments, so logically equivalent inputs such as "src/./File.cs" and "src/File.cs" compare unequal. Applicable analyzer findings can consequently disappear from the projected evidence.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize repository-relative paths consistently before comparison, including redundant separators and dot segments. Reject paths that escape the repository rather than resolving them silently. Keep comparison semantics explicitly aligned with the repository's cross-platform path policy.

findings.title: Conflicting sensor configurations use an implicit first-wins policy
findings.description: DistinctBy silently retains the first configuration for a sensor ID and drops all later entries, even when their Configuration values differ. The effective scan therefore depends on input ordering, and a caller receives no indication that part of its requested configuration was ignored.
findings.recommendation: Require sensor IDs to be unique and report conflicting duplicates, or define and document an explicit merge or precedence policy. If identical duplicates are intentionally accepted, verify their configurations are equivalent before deduplicating them.

grade.rationale: The design is generally readable and dependency injection supports testing, but scope handling can silently scan the wrong target, ESLint availability checks the wrong executable, and several expected parsing and filesystem failures escape the structured sensor-result contract.

observations.summary: The implementation is clear overall, but it has correctness and resilience gaps around analyzer probing, path-scoped requests, diagnostic parsing, and report persistence. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied.

findings.title: ESLint availability probe never checks ESLint
findings.description: The ESLint sensor configures the shared probe as `node --version`. A system with Node installed but no usable ESLint installation is therefore reported as available, and the returned tool version describes Node rather than the analyzer. This can defer a predictable configuration failure until the scan runs.
findings.recommendation: Probe the actual ESLint executable used by the scan, such as a repository-local `npx --no-install eslint --version`, and record the resulting ESLint version. If Node is also relevant, record it as a separate prerequisite version.

findings.title: A path-scoped request without a path scans the repository root
findings.description: When `Scope` is `Path` but `request.Path` is null or whitespace, the target falls back to the repository root. The sensor can consequently return repository-wide findings for a request represented in provenance as a missing path, violating the requested scope and potentially producing misleading evidence.
findings.recommendation: Validate the requested scope before deriving the target. Return a failed `SensorScanResult` when a path-scoped request lacks a non-empty path, and explicitly reject unsupported scope values.

findings.title: Malformed diagnostic fields can abort the scan
findings.description: Compiler output is converted with `Path.GetFullPath` and `int.Parse` without per-diagnostic validation. An invalid path or an oversized line or column number can throw, escaping `RunAsync` instead of being ignored or returned as a structured analyzer failure.
findings.recommendation: Use `int.TryParse` with explicit bounds, catch path-normalization exceptions per match, and either skip malformed diagnostic lines or return a structured failure containing a bounded output detail.

findings.title: Report persistence failures bypass the sensor result contract
findings.description: Directory creation and report writing occur outside the guarded command-execution block. Common failures such as an inaccessible directory, a read-only repository, or another I/O error therefore throw from `RunAsync` rather than producing an unavailable result. Cancellation should still propagate, but ordinary persistence failures should be translated consistently.
findings.recommendation: Wrap report-directory creation and writing in narrowly scoped handling for `IOException`, `UnauthorizedAccessException`, and relevant path exceptions, returning a structured failure while allowing `OperationCanceledException` to propagate.

grade.rationale: The models are generally clear and immutable, and catalogue precedence and hashing are straightforward. The main weaknesses are incomplete validation of deserialized data, acceptance of undefined numeric enum values, externally mutable canonical serialization settings, and limited file context in parse failures.

observations.summary: The implementation is well structured and the available .NET build analyzer reported no findings. Four robustness issues remain around malformed catalogue handling and stable serialization. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied.

findings.title: Catalogue validation is not total for deserialized null values
findings.description: Nullable-reference annotations are not enforced by System.Text.Json. An Entries array containing null reaches GroupBy and dereferences entry.Id, producing NullReferenceException instead of the resolver's documented-style JsonException. Additionally, a missing or null DeterministicRuleIds member is not rejected and can escape validation despite being declared non-nullable.
findings.recommendation: Validate that every entry is non-null before accessing its members, then validate every required collection, including DeterministicRuleIds, and reject null or blank collection elements. Return a JsonException that identifies the source and invalid field.

findings.title: Undefined numeric enum values are accepted
findings.description: JsonStringEnumConverter allows integer values by default. Consequently, an external catalogue can deserialize values such as severity 999, and Validate does not check Enum.IsDefined, leaving downstream code with an unsupported AttackSeverity value.
findings.recommendation: Construct the converter with allowIntegerValues set to false and, for defense in depth, validate enum-backed catalogue fields with Enum.IsDefined.

findings.title: Canonical hashing depends on publicly exposed mutable options
findings.description: Options exposes the same JsonSerializerOptions instance used for hashes and catalogue parsing. A consumer can modify it before first serialization, changing hashes and accepted JSON process-wide; after first use, mutation instead throws because the options become read-only. This creates order-dependent global behavior.
findings.recommendation: Keep the canonical options private and expose a defensive copy only if consumers need similar settings. Explicitly make the internal instance read-only before publishing or using it for hashes.

findings.title: Catalogue syntax errors omit explicit source-file context
findings.description: ReadFile lets deserialization exceptions propagate directly. JsonException can report a JSON path and byte position, but it does not inherently identify which global or project catalogue file was being read, making failures harder to diagnose when multiple sources are resolved.
findings.recommendation: Catch JsonException in ReadFile and rethrow a new JsonException that includes the supplied path while preserving the original exception as InnerException.

grade.rationale: The service has a coherent domain model and useful validation, hashing, and projection structure, but several correctness hazards can make coverage appear current when deterministic results or relevant code have changed. Failed submissions can also mutate finding lifecycle state, and malformed persisted data is not handled consistently.

observations.summary: The most serious issues are stale deterministic observations being reused by default, syntax-insensitive source extraction that can omit meaningful code changes, and finding-state mutations occurring before a submission is fully validated and durably appended. Test coverage is unknown. The supplied dotnet-build analyzer reported no findings; the ESLint analyzer was unavailable and is not relevant to this C# file.

findings.title: Existing deterministic observations prevent detection of new sensor results
findings.description: With the default recheckDeterministic value, the presence of any prior deterministic observation skips the boundary/attack pair before current findings and deterministic inputs are compared. A prior pass can therefore remain an authoritative mechanical pass when the inventory later contains a finding, especially when the boundary, catalogue, and prompt hashes are unchanged. The later alreadyCurrent comparison cannot protect against this because it is unreachable for such pairs.
findings.recommendation: Compute the current deterministic inputs on every build and use the alreadyCurrent comparison to avoid duplicate appends. If sensor execution must be optional, distinguish disabling the sensor from forcing an otherwise identical rerun, and include the inventory sensor version in freshness identity.

findings.title: Lexical delimiter counting can omit meaningful covered code
findings.description: StatementAtLine and MethodBody count delimiters without recognizing strings, character literals, comments, interpolated expressions, or nested language constructs. Method discovery can also match an invocation or comment rather than a declaration. A brace or semicolon inside text can terminate extraction early, allowing later security-relevant edits in the actual handler to leave CoveredCodeHash unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Use Roslyn syntax trees to locate the declaration containing the configured line and named handlers, then hash normalized syntax spans. If heuristic extraction must remain, treat ambiguous or unbalanced parsing as an explicit incomplete snapshot rather than a valid coverage hash.

findings.title: A rejected submission can still mutate finding lifecycle state
findings.description: RecordAsync updates the finding state store before constructing and validating the ledger observation. For example, a NotYetChecked submission, a non-finding submission carrying finding fields, or a submission with negative token counts can cause MergeReviewAsync to close prior findings and then fail when AppendAsync validates the observation. Snapshot, Git, cancellation, or append failures can create the same split state.
findings.recommendation: Validate every submission and resulting observation invariant before any persistent mutation. Then coordinate the lifecycle update and ledger append transactionally, or introduce an idempotent operation record and recovery procedure so partial failure cannot leave the stores inconsistent.

findings.title: Malformed ledger objects bypass line-specific JSON error handling
findings.description: JSON deserialization can produce an observation whose Reviewer, TokenCost, or Evidence member is null despite non-nullable annotations. Validate dereferences those members directly, producing NullReferenceException. ReadAsync catches only JsonException, so callers lose the documented line-specific corruption diagnostic and receive an unexpected exception type.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly reject null nested objects and collections before reading their members. Keep all persisted-data validation failures as JsonException so ReadAsync can consistently wrap them with the ledger line number.

findings.title: Repository confinement check does not prevent symlink or junction escapes
findings.description: ResolveWithinRoot validates only the lexical full path. A path beneath the repository can be a symbolic link or junction targeting a file outside it, and File.ReadAllTextAsync will follow that link. This violates the method's repository-boundary guarantee and can incorporate out-of-scope source into coverage hashes.
findings.recommendation: Resolve existing path components through links and verify the final target remains beneath the canonical repository root. Define and test the desired behavior for repository roots that are themselves filesystem roots.

findings.title: Boundary-targeted findings can crash when they have no locations
findings.description: FindingTargetsBoundary can accept a finding solely because its JSON evidence contains the boundaryId. RefreshDeterministicAsync then unconditionally reads finding.Locations[0] when building lifecycle identities. A finding with valid boundary evidence but an empty Locations collection therefore causes IndexOutOfRangeException and aborts matrix construction.
findings.recommendation: Validate deterministic findings before use and obtain the path with FirstOrDefault, falling back to the boundary path when boundaryId evidence is authoritative. Otherwise reject the finding with a descriptive validation error that identifies it.

grade.rationale: The implementation is substantial and readable, but several core heuristics violate the sensor's stated conservative contract. Authentication and authorization can be overstated, security findings can consequently be suppressed, and detected boundaries can be silently discarded. Source-discovery failures and repository-containment gaps further undermine inventory completeness and trustworthiness.

observations.summary: The sensor compiles according to the supplied analyzer evidence and has deterministic ordering, stable serialization, cancellation during file reads, and generally clear data models. Its main weakness is unsound inference: repository-wide or file-wide string matches are treated as endpoint-specific proof, authorization checks omit authenticated-but-unauthorized boundaries, and several parsing shortcuts can either suppress real findings or manufacture incorrect facts. No test coverage evidence was supplied, so coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Authentication middleware is treated as an endpoint requirement
findings.description: For every /api route in a file, the presence of StartsWithSegments("/api") and either Authenticate(context) or UseAuthentication() anywhere in that file upgrades the route to authenticated. UseAuthentication only populates the principal; it does not reject anonymous callers, and the substring checks do not establish control flow, ordering, or applicability to this endpoint. DeriveAuthorization similarly promotes every matching API route to repository-scoped when a recognized CanAccess call appears anywhere in the file. This can suppress the sensor's most important security findings despite the class contract promising that unproved facts remain unknown.
findings.recommendation: Build endpoint-specific evidence from syntax or semantic analysis. Treat authentication middleware as infrastructure only, require an endpoint authorization policy or a proven rejecting middleware branch, and associate repository-access checks with the actual handler control flow before upgrading either fact.

findings.title: Missing-authorization finding only examines authentication
findings.description: The rule titled "Inbound boundary has no derived authorization" tests Authentication.Value but never Authorization.Value. A boundary classified as authenticated with authorization none, unknown, or authenticated-only produces no missing-authorization finding. This is especially damaging because earlier broad heuristics readily upgrade authentication.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate authentication and authorization independently. Emit an authentication finding when credentials are not required and an authorization finding whenever Authorization.Value is none, unknown, or otherwise below the policy required for the boundary.

findings.title: Explicit ASP.NET parameter binding attributes are discarded
findings.description: ParseDotNetInputs removes all attributes from parameter before checking for FromHeader, FromBody, or FromRoute. Those checks can therefore never succeed. Parameters are instead classified using route-name and type heuristics, producing incorrect boundary input sources and potentially misleading downstream sink findings.
findings.recommendation: Extract binding metadata before removing attributes, or parse the parameter with Roslyn. Preserve attribute arguments as well, since attributes can rename the externally visible parameter.

findings.title: ID-based deduplication silently drops distinct boundaries
findings.description: Entries are deduplicated by StableId before mechanical checks. HTTP IDs contain only method and normalized route, so identical routes in different applications, files, frameworks, host groups, or duplicated registrations collapse into one entry. The retained entry's authentication, limits, side effects, and location depend on analyzer insertion order, and findings associated with discarded registrations are never evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Include application identity and source location in registration IDs, or merge duplicate registrations conservatively by retaining every location and selecting the least-protective fact. Run checks before any presentation-only grouping.

findings.title: Unreadable sources disappear without marking the inventory incomplete
findings.description: IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, and DecoderFallbackException are swallowed without recording a finding or completeness state. Contrary to the comment, facts from an unreadable file do not remain unknown; the file and all boundaries it may contain are absent. Consumers cannot distinguish a complete inventory from a partial scan.
findings.recommendation: Record a structured scan diagnostic for every skipped file and expose an incomplete status in the result or inventory. Include the path and failure category without leaking sensitive exception details, and let policy decide whether persistence is allowed for incomplete repository scans.

findings.title: Any mention of origin is reported as an origin check
findings.description: A browser-message receiver is classified as origin-checked when its captured statement merely contains the text origin. Logging event.origin, copying it, comparing it without rejecting, or using an unrelated identifier such as original is therefore treated as authorization. This can prevent the missing-authorization check from describing the actual weakness accurately.
findings.recommendation: Require a recognized comparison of event.origin against a fixed or configured allowlist together with a rejecting control-flow branch. Otherwise retain authorization as unknown; use none only when absence is established confidently.

findings.title: Recursive enumeration can follow directory links outside the repository
findings.description: ResolveTarget performs lexical containment only, and recursive enumeration pushes every non-ignored child directory without rejecting symbolic links, junctions, or other reparse points. A repository-controlled link can cause the sensor to read files outside the repository and emit paths containing parent traversal segments, potentially exposing unrelated source or configuration in persisted evidence.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate each traversed directory against the canonical repository root, skip reparse points by default, and maintain a visited-directory identity set to prevent cycles. Record skipped links as diagnostics when they affect completeness.

findings.title: Expression-bodied controller actions can be assigned another method's body
findings.description: The controller analyzer searches for the next opening brace anywhere after an action signature and only verifies that it is inside the controller. For an expression-bodied or abstract action, that brace may belong to a later action or nested construct. Side effects and response behavior from the unrelated block are then attributed to the wrong endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Parse controller members with Roslyn, or at minimum detect an expression-body token and stop at that member's terminating semicolon while bounding brace searches before the next member declaration.

grade.rationale: The command is generally clear and handles expected operational failures consistently, but its mode validation has a concrete gap and its hard-coded collaborators make orchestration behavior unnecessarily difficult to test in isolation.

observations.summary: The implementation is readable and mostly robust. The main correctness issue is that an explicitly supplied `--last 1` is accepted alongside `--base`, despite those options representing mutually exclusive modes. Testability is also reduced by constructing every reviewer, provider, and service directly inside `RunAsync`. No coverage conclusions were drawn because coverage data is unavailable.

findings.title: Explicit `--last 1` bypasses mutually exclusive mode validation
findings.description: The parser stores only the numeric value of `--last`, whose default is also `1`. Consequently, `--base <commit> --last 1` passes this condition even though the error message and usage syntax establish `--base` and `--last` as different provider modes. This makes validation depend on the supplied value rather than whether the option was present.
findings.recommendation: Track whether `--last` was explicitly supplied, such as with a `lastSet` boolean, and reject any explicit `--last` whenever `--base` is present regardless of its value.

findings.title: Command orchestration is coupled to concrete dependencies
findings.description: `RunAsync` directly constructs the agent adapter, review service, and Git provider. Unit tests therefore cannot substitute deterministic fakes to cover success, regression, empty-result, JSON, and collaborator-failure paths without invoking repository-facing implementations.
findings.recommendation: Move the orchestration into an internal overload or instance command that accepts the change-set provider, review service, and reviewer factory as dependencies, while retaining the current public method as the production composition root.

grade.rationale: The contract is structured clearly and serialization is deterministic, but validation is too shallow for an evidence format containing several duplicated representations. Malformed JSON can also escape validation through null-reference failures and inconsistent exception types.

observations.summary: The primary risk is that deserialized evidence may contain mutually contradictory subject, review, agent, and finding data while still passing validation. Input failures are also not consistently reported as JSON contract errors. Build evidence reported no findings; test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Validation permits contradictory evidence projections
findings.description: Each entry contains overlapping representations: Subject duplicates repository and change-set commits, AgentEvidence projects Review.Judgement, and Findings projects Review.Delta.Findings. Validation compares only Subject.ResultSha with the review result commit. A document can therefore pass validation while naming a different repository or base/head commits, reporting incompatible agent status or provenance, or presenting finding envelopes that disagree with the embedded review delta. Consumers choosing different projections can reach different conclusions from the same accepted evidence document.
findings.recommendation: Define all cross-object invariants and enforce them during validation. At minimum, bind the subject repository and every commit to the document and change set, validate agent evidence against the judgement, and verify finding changes against the delta. Prefer deriving redundant projections after deserialization or validating against a single canonical entry-construction routine to prevent the checks from drifting.

findings.title: Explicit null members bypass required-member guarantees and crash validation
findings.description: C# non-nullability and required members do not prevent JSON from explicitly supplying null. A null policy, reviews collection, review entry, subject, or embedded review can consequently reach this code and cause NullReferenceException rather than a controlled contract-validation failure.
findings.recommendation: Validate every externally deserialized object and collection before dereferencing it, including collection elements and nested review state. Throw JsonException with the relevant property path. Consider separate input DTOs or custom converters if stronger construction-time guarantees are needed.

findings.title: Malformed serialized hashes surface as ArgumentException
findings.description: ValidateSha256 throws ArgumentException for invalid values regardless of call context. Deserialize therefore exposes malformed document content as an API-argument failure, while other invalid document fields produce JsonException. A null hash additionally fails at value.Length with NullReferenceException.
findings.recommendation: Make the hash validator null-safe and allow callers to select the appropriate exception type, or translate its failure to JsonException in document validation while retaining ArgumentException for Create arguments. Include the JSON property path in deserialization errors.

grade.rationale: The file is concise, consistently named, and provides clear immutable-looking contracts, but some public models admit invalid states and the shared NotRun instance exposes mutable collection storage.

observations.summary: The model layer is generally clear and maintainable. The principal correctness risk is that ChangeSetQuery accepts nonsensical values without a validation boundary. A smaller reliability issue is that ChangeJudgement.NotRun shares an array through an IReadOnlyList interface, allowing callers to mutate global state by casting it. Test coverage is unknown; the supplied .NET build evidence reported no findings, while the unavailable ESLint result is not applicable to this C# file.

findings.title: ChangeSetQuery permits invalid requests
findings.description: The public positional constructor accepts an empty repository root, an empty head revision, and zero or negative Count values. These states have no meaningful interpretation in the provider contract, so every IChangeSetProvider implementation must independently validate them or may produce inconsistent behavior, confusing downstream errors, or invalid command arguments.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the invariants at a single boundary, such as a validating constructor or factory: require non-blank RepositoryRoot and HeadRevision and require Count to be greater than zero. If unrestricted values are intentional, document their exact semantics in the interface contract.

findings.title: NotRun exposes mutable shared collection storage
findings.description: NotRun is a process-wide singleton whose Aspects value is created as an array and exposed only nominally as IReadOnlyList. A caller can cast that value back to an array or IList and replace elements, permanently changing the shared default for later callers and potentially making tests order-dependent.
findings.recommendation: Store the aspects in a genuinely immutable collection such as ImmutableArray<ChangeJudgementAspect>, or return a fresh ChangeJudgement instance when requested. If retaining IReadOnlyList, wrap storage so callers cannot recover and mutate the underlying collection.

grade.rationale: The service is generally well structured and deterministic, but several edge cases can produce incorrect review documents, including collapsed HTTP boundaries, corrupted dotfile paths, misleading summaries, and an unsafe persistence path. Error handling also obscures some Git failures and inconsistently wraps malformed metadata.

observations.summary: The implementation has clear decomposition and sensible immutable result models, but its correctness degrades for common repository constructs such as multiple attribute-routed endpoints and dotfiles. Persistence-path validation and more precise failure classification should be addressed before relying on the generated review artifacts as authoritative evidence.

findings.title: Commit metadata can escape the review output directory
findings.description: The persisted filename is constructed directly from MergeCommit or HeadCommit. MergeCommit is not validated by the preceding metadata loads, and a provider-supplied value containing rooted or parent-directory path components can cause GetPath to resolve outside `.quality/changes`. Even benign ref-like identifiers containing separators unexpectedly create nested paths.
findings.recommendation: Require a canonical hexadecimal object ID before using it as a filename, or derive a filesystem-safe deterministic name by hashing the identifier. Resolve the resulting path and verify that it remains beneath the intended changes directory.

findings.title: Multiple attribute-routed endpoints in one file collapse into one boundary
findings.description: A parameterless attribute such as `[HttpGet]` is assigned the common name `(attribute route)`, and the identity contains only the file path, HTTP method, and that name. Consequently, multiple parameterless attributes using the same verb in one file receive identical identities. The final DistinctBy call drops all but one, so new, removed, or changed endpoints can be omitted from the boundary delta.
findings.recommendation: Include a stable enclosing controller/action identity or another syntax-derived declaration key in the boundary identity. Do not use the source line alone if identities must survive harmless line movement.

findings.title: Path normalization corrupts leading-dot filenames
findings.description: `TrimStart('.', '/')` removes every leading dot and slash rather than only a conventional `./` prefix. For example, `.editorconfig` becomes `editorconfig`. Metadata for dotfiles can therefore fail touched-path matching, and staleness checks can read the wrong path or report the reviewed input as missing.
findings.recommendation: Normalize separators and remove only explicitly recognized prefixes such as `./`; preserve leading dots that are part of a repository filename.

findings.title: All Git read failures are treated as missing files
findings.description: When allowMissing is true, ReadFileAsync catches every ChangeReviewException from GitPlumbing and returns null. This does not distinguish an absent path from an invalid revision, repository corruption, process failure, or another operational error. Callers can consequently emit false missing/stale evidence or silently omit boundary and economy data.
findings.recommendation: Have GitPlumbing expose a typed missing-path result or inspect a structured exit classification, and suppress only the expected object/path-not-found case. Propagate other failures with their context intact.

findings.title: Missing grade fields cause an uncontextualized null-reference failure
findings.description: The parser verifies that `grade` is an object but then null-forgives its `score` and `band` children. If either field is absent, dereferencing the null node throws NullReferenceException, which is not covered by the contextual parsing catch. This leaks an implementation exception without identifying the metadata path and revision.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly validate the required grade fields and their types before constructing MetaSnapshot, then throw ChangeReviewException with the metadata path and revision for every schema violation.

findings.title: Valid quality changes can produce an empty summary
findings.description: BuildSummary adds facts for regressions and resolved findings but omits grade improvements, removed boundaries, and both positive and negative coverage changes. Those conditions can independently set HasQualityDelta and determine the verdict, producing output such as `Improved: .` or `Regression: .`.
findings.recommendation: Add summary facts for every condition used by DetermineVerdict and HasQualityDelta. As a defensive fallback, emit a meaningful generic sentence whenever the fact list remains empty.

grade.rationale: The implementation supports several coverage formats and has generally clear decomposition, but aggregation can produce incorrect branch coverage, path identity is unreliable, freshness can be overstated, and external conversion can hang indefinitely. Error handling around persisted and malformed data also needs strengthening.

observations.summary: The principal correctness risk is that branch observations from overlapping reports are appended rather than merged, producing misleading totals and percentages. Other material issues include indefinite subprocess waits, invalid snapshots escaping deserialization, path-normalization collisions, uncertain commits being labeled current, and malformed XML being misdiagnosed as native coverage.

findings.title: Overlapping reports double-count branch points
findings.description: All reports share one accumulator, but branch observations are appended without a branch identity or merge rule. If two reports contain the same instrumented branch, it is counted twice; a branch uncovered in one test shard and covered in another becomes 1/2 instead of the correct aggregate 1/1. Line observations avoid this problem by merging hits by line number.
findings.recommendation: Represent branches using a stable format-specific identity, such as file plus line, block, and branch ordinal, and merge their covered state with logical OR across reports. If a format cannot provide identity, define and document a conservative deduplication policy rather than blindly appending observations.

findings.title: Coverage conversion can wait indefinitely or deadlock
findings.description: The converter redirects both output streams, consumes neither, and then calls WaitForExit without a timeout or cancellation. A child that fills either pipe or stops responding can block the scan indefinitely, and the RunAsync cancellation token cannot interrupt it.
findings.recommendation: Drain stdout and stderr concurrently, use WaitForExitAsync with the scan cancellation token and a bounded timeout, and terminate the process tree on timeout or cancellation. Propagate the token through parsing and conversion APIs.

findings.title: Deserialized snapshots are accepted without structural validation
findings.description: Successful JSON deserialization does not guarantee that required record properties are present or non-null. A syntactically valid file that omits or nulls Files, Reports, or uncovered-line collections is returned and can later fail with NullReferenceException. Unsupported schema versions and invalid coverage counts are also silently accepted.
findings.recommendation: Deserialize into a nullable value and validate the schema version, required collections, non-negative counts, covered-versus-total invariants, and required strings before returning it. Treat validation failures consistently as unavailable or return a diagnostic result that distinguishes corruption from absence.

findings.title: Path normalization can conflate distinct files
findings.description: TrimStart('.', '/') removes every leading dot or slash rather than only a leading './'. Consequently, paths such as .github/workflow.yml and github/workflow.yml normalize to the same value, while parent components are also erased. In addition, Ordinal matching remains case-sensitive on Windows, so differently cased spellings of the same file can fail to match or be accumulated separately.
findings.recommendation: Create one canonical repository-path abstraction that normalizes separators, removes only explicit current-directory prefixes, rejects parent traversal, and uses an operating-system-appropriate comparer. Apply it consistently when parsing, accumulating, projecting, and generating evidence.

findings.title: Coverage is labeled current when freshness cannot be established
findings.description: The state becomes stale only when both commits are present and unequal; every other matched snapshot is labeled current. If Git is unavailable, the snapshot lacks a commit, or the caller cannot determine the current commit, the code asserts current coverage despite having no basis for that conclusion. Evidence uses the same logic and can omit an important uncertainty.
findings.recommendation: Use a distinct freshness state such as unknown or unverified whenever either commit is unavailable. Reserve current for two known equal commits, and apply the same classification helper in both ForPath and Evidence.

findings.title: Every XML parse failure is reported as unavailable native coverage conversion
findings.description: Any XmlException is interpreted as evidence that the input is a native binary .coverage file. If conversion fails, the resulting exception claims both that the report is native and that dotnet-coverage is unavailable, even when the input is merely malformed or the converter exists but returned an error. This hides the actionable cause and discards converter diagnostics.
findings.recommendation: Attempt native conversion only for .coverage inputs or after positively identifying the binary format. Preserve malformed-XML errors for textual reports, and capture the converter exit code and stderr so conversion failures can be reported accurately.

grade.rationale: The implementation is well structured and reasonably testable, but a vulnerability scanner must avoid silent false negatives and uncontrolled traversal. Unsupported JSON is accepted as a clean scan, npm versions can be misattributed, path validation is unsafe on case-sensitive systems, directory links can escape or cycle, and cancellation can leave scanner processes running.

observations.summary: The code is readable and separates command execution from parsing effectively. The principal risks are fail-open parsing, inaccurate npm evidence, unsafe filesystem traversal, incomplete exception handling, abandoned child processes, and all-or-nothing failure behavior that discards useful results. Build analysis reported no findings; test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Unrecognized scanner JSON is treated as a clean scan
findings.description: ParseDotNet returns no findings whenever the projects property is absent or has the wrong type. ParseNpm similarly returns no findings when neither supported audit structure is present. RunAsync consequently reports the scan as available and clean even if a tool changes its schema or emits an unexpected successful response, creating a silent false negative.
findings.recommendation: Validate a supported schema and required root fields before parsing. Throw a dedicated parse/schema exception for unrecognized output so RunAsync reports the scan as unavailable rather than clean; add fixtures for malformed and future-version payloads.

findings.title: npm findings can report the wrong installed package version
findings.description: ReadNpmVersions records only top-level node_modules entries and stores a single version per package name. npm lockfiles can contain several versions of the same package at different nested paths, so ParseNpm may attach a top-level version to an advisory affecting a nested version, or report no version despite having exact node information. This makes the title, evidence, remediation context, and fingerprint inaccurate.
findings.recommendation: Use the audit entry's affected nodes and resolve each node path against the lockfile packages object. Emit findings for the distinct affected installed versions, or avoid asserting an exact version when it cannot be mapped reliably.

findings.title: Path containment check can accept a sibling directory on case-sensitive systems
findings.description: ResolveTarget always compares paths with OrdinalIgnoreCase. On a case-sensitive platform, a request such as ../Repo can therefore pass validation for a repository rooted at /repo when /Repo is a separate existing sibling directory, allowing the sensor to scan outside the requested repository.
findings.recommendation: Use platform-appropriate path comparison and validate containment by examining a normalized relative path. Reject rooted relative results and any result equal to .. or beginning with a .. directory segment. Address symbolic-link containment separately.

findings.title: Recursive discovery follows directory links without containment or cycle protection
findings.description: FindFiles recursively pushes every non-ignored directory without detecting symbolic links, junctions, previously visited directories, or resolved paths outside the repository. A link can cause external projects to be scanned and commands to run against them; a link to an ancestor can also create unbounded traversal.
findings.recommendation: Define and enforce a link policy. Prefer skipping reparse-point/symbolic-link directories; otherwise resolve link targets, require them to remain under the canonical repository root, and track canonical directory identities to prevent cycles.

findings.title: Cancellation can leave the scanner subprocess running
findings.description: If WaitForExitAsync is cancelled, RunAsync exits and disposes the Process object but does not terminate the underlying child process. A cancelled dotnet or npm audit can therefore continue consuming CPU, holding files, or spawning descendants after the scan has ended.
findings.recommendation: Catch cancellation after a successful start, terminate the process tree when it is still running, wait for termination, and then rethrow the original OperationCanceledException. Ensure output-reading tasks are observed during cleanup.

findings.title: Common filesystem traversal failures bypass the unavailable result
findings.description: Directory enumeration can throw UnauthorizedAccessException and related filesystem exceptions, but RunAsync only converts IOException and a small set of other exceptions into an unavailable result. A repository containing an inaccessible directory can therefore fault the entire sensor call unexpectedly rather than returning structured availability information.
findings.recommendation: Handle expected traversal failures explicitly, either by converting them to an unavailable result with the affected path or by adopting and documenting a safe skip policy. Keep cancellation and programming errors unmasked.

findings.title: One unavailable tool or failed target discards all viable scan results
findings.description: The default configuration requires both tool probes to succeed before any scan runs, and any subsequent project or lockfile failure immediately returns an unavailable result whose findings collection is always empty. Consequently, a missing npm installation can suppress valid .NET analysis, and a late failure discards findings already collected from earlier targets.
findings.recommendation: Represent per-ecosystem and per-target completion explicitly. Preserve findings from successful scans, report diagnostics for failed portions, and mark the result incomplete; alternatively scan only ecosystems detected in the repository unless the configuration explicitly requires others.

grade.rationale: The implementation has a clear deterministic identity scheme, but several behaviors undermine its stated trust boundary: unresolved locations remain persisted, invalid ranges are converted into apparently observed evidence, malformed agent JSON can abort processing through unchecked node access, and Windows absolute paths pass the repository-relative validation.

observations.summary: Deterministic hashing and line-ending normalization are straightforward, but validation and evidence handling need stronger guarantees before persisted identities and anchors can be considered trustworthy. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage data was supplied; the successful dotnet-build analyzer reported no findings.

findings.title: Locations outside the reviewed subjects remain in persisted findings
findings.description: When a location does not match normalizedSubjects, the loop skips processing it but never removes it from the finding's locations array. If another location resolves, the finding is retained together with the skipped, unvalidated location. This contradicts the comment that the location is invalidated and allows unnormalized paths or unverified ranges to remain in the completed review document.
findings.recommendation: Build a new locations array containing only successfully resolved and validated locations, or explicitly remove each rejected location before persisting the finding. Use that validated collection when choosing the primary location.

findings.title: Invalid ranges are transformed into trusted observed evidence
findings.description: ExtractSnippet clamps every supplied coordinate into the file and even replaces a reversed same-line range with the entire line. Thus a wildly incorrect agent location can be silently moved to unrelated source text. AttachRunnerCapturedEvidence then labels that generated span as observed, giving fabricated location precision the same status as an originally valid range.
findings.recommendation: Validate ranges before extraction and reject locations whose coordinates are out of bounds or reversed. If limited tolerance is required, retain the original coordinates, record that a correction occurred, and do not classify the resulting source span as observed without an independent match.

findings.title: Malformed finding JSON causes uncontrolled runtime exceptions
findings.description: The public entry point treats agent-produced JSON as structurally valid through null-forgiving operators and calls such as AsArray, AsObject, and GetValue. Missing nodes, incorrect node types, or invalid scalar values therefore throw NullReferenceException or JSON conversion exceptions and can abort processing of the entire response, despite the surrounding design attempting to preserve usable findings.
findings.recommendation: Validate the findings collection, each finding, every location, and all range coordinates with TryGetPropertyValue and explicit node/type checks. Either reject malformed input with a contextual ReviewResponseException or discard only the malformed finding according to a documented policy.

findings.title: Windows drive-qualified paths bypass repository-relative validation
findings.description: NormalizePath rejects leading slashes and '..' segments but accepts drive-qualified paths such as C:/Projects/repository/file.cs. Such a path is absolute on Windows and violates the method's repository-relative invariant. If subjectContents contains a similarly formed key, it can also participate in identity and evidence generation.
findings.recommendation: Reject rooted and drive-qualified paths using a platform-independent repository-path check, including drive-letter prefixes and UNC forms. Also reject empty paths and consider canonicalizing redundant '.' and empty segments before comparison and hashing.

grade.rationale: The projection is readable and compact, but it is not idempotent, does not enforce state expiration, can retain stale state metadata, and assumes optional grade fields have exactly the expected shape.

observations.summary: The implementation has a clear structure and avoids mutating its input directly. Its principal correctness risk is that applying the projection more than once repeatedly inflates the effective score and appends duplicate rationale text. Expiring states and previously projected state metadata also require explicit handling. Build analysis reported no .NET findings; test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Applying the projection repeatedly inflates the effective grade
findings.description: The method treats the current grade score as the raw score, overwrites it with the adjusted score, and appends to the current rationale. If its output is supplied to Apply again, the adjustment is applied to an already-adjusted value—for example, 80 can become 90 and then 95—and the explanatory sentence is duplicated. A projection should produce the same result when applied repeatedly to the same findings and states.
findings.recommendation: Preserve an immutable base score and rationale, or make the effective grade separate fields. Calculate exclusively from those base values and replace, rather than append to, projection-generated rationale content.

findings.title: Expired finding states are still applied
findings.description: The effective state is selected solely from State and never checks ExpiresAt. Consequently, an expired waiver or false-positive state remains excluded from the grade indefinitely, despite its expiration timestamp being exposed in the projection.
findings.recommendation: Determine whether the record is active before selecting its state, using an injected clock or an explicit evaluation timestamp. Treat expired records according to the intended policy, typically as Open, while optionally retaining their history separately.

findings.title: State metadata from an earlier projection can remain stale
findings.description: Apply clones all existing finding properties but only writes stateAuthor, stateReason, stateTimestamp, and stateExpiresAt when corresponding values are present. If previously projected metadata is processed after a state is removed, those properties remain even though the finding is now Open. Likewise, changing a state from expiring to non-expiring leaves the old stateExpiresAt value in place.
findings.recommendation: Remove all projection-owned state metadata from each cloned finding before applying the current state, then add only the properties supported by the current record.

findings.title: Missing or non-string grade rationale causes an exception
findings.description: The null-forgiving operator only suppresses compiler diagnostics; it does not protect the GetValue<string>() call. Metadata with a valid numeric score but a missing, null, or non-string rationale throws after the effective score has been calculated instead of returning a usable projection.
findings.recommendation: Use TryGetValue<string> and either omit the suffix, initialize a default rationale, or validate the grade object explicitly before changing it.

grade.rationale: The store has a sound overall structure, injected clock, deterministic serialization, and coordinated writes, but several edge cases undermine correctness and resilience: optimistic concurrency can miss updates, merge inputs can create an unreadable document, expiry can advance revisions inconsistently, and lock acquisition can wait indefinitely.

observations.summary: The implementation is generally clear and thoughtfully organized, but its persistence boundary needs stronger validation and failure handling. The most consequential risks are an unbounded retry loop around the lock file and timestamp-based conflict detection that is not guaranteed to distinguish successive writes. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied.

findings.title: Timestamps are not reliable optimistic-concurrency tokens
findings.description: SetAsync accepts the update when expectedTimestamp equals the current record timestamp, then assigns Timestamp from the injected clock. Two successive updates can therefore have the same timestamp when the clock has limited resolution or is fixed in tests. A second client holding the original timestamp can then overwrite the first update without receiving FindingStateConflictException.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit monotonically increasing record version or the document revision as the concurrency token. If the API must retain timestamps, do not rely on them alone for compare-and-swap behavior.

findings.title: MergeReviewAsync can persist data that LoadAsync subsequently rejects
findings.description: Unlike SetAsync, MergeReviewAsync does not validate or normalize author, and it does not validate identity fields before NewRecord copies them into the document. A blank author, malformed fingerprint, or blank finding metadata can be saved successfully, after which the next LoadAsync call rejects the store as invalid. Null current or previous collections also fail with incidental NullReferenceException rather than argument validation.
findings.recommendation: Validate collection arguments, author length and whitespace, and every FindingIdentityRecord at the start of MergeReviewAsync. Apply the same normalization and invariants used by SetAsync and LoadAsync before modifying or saving the document.

findings.title: MergeReviewAsync advances the revision twice for an expiry-only change
findings.description: ReopenExpired returns a document whose revision has already been incremented. MergeReviewAsync then sets changed from expiredChanged and, even when the merge itself changes nothing, constructs another document using document.Revision + 1. Consequently, the same expiry advances the revision once when triggered by ReadAsync but twice when triggered by MergeReviewAsync, making revision semantics dependent on the entry point.
findings.recommendation: Have ReopenExpired return changed records without changing the revision, and increment exactly once at the persistence boundary, or track merge changes separately and avoid the second increment when expiry is the only change.

findings.title: Lock acquisition retries every IOException indefinitely
findings.description: The lock loop treats every IOException as evidence that another writer owns the lock. With the default non-cancelable token, a stale lock file or a persistent filesystem error can make every operation wait forever while polling every 25 milliseconds. Some IOExceptions are permanent and should be surfaced rather than hidden as contention.
findings.recommendation: Retry only failures positively identified as lock contention, impose a configurable timeout or stale-lock policy, and propagate other IOExceptions with lock-path context. Consider a lock mechanism whose ownership and abandonment behavior can be determined reliably.

findings.title: A null finding entry bypasses controlled JSON validation
findings.description: JSON can contain a null element in the findings array despite the non-nullable C# annotation. The duplicate check dereferences record.Fingerprint before the later validity check, so such input throws NullReferenceException instead of a descriptive JsonException. The later predicate would also dereference the record.
findings.recommendation: Reject null collection elements explicitly before grouping or accessing their properties, and report the failure as JsonException with the other document-validation errors.

grade.rationale: The models are concise and readable, but they permit internally inconsistent reports and invalid path indexing without any local validation. These weaknesses can shift failures into downstream consumers and complicate reliable testing.

observations.summary: The immutable record-based design is clear and generally maintainable. The principal risks are unenforced cross-field invariants in FlowFinding and FlowReviewReport; no test coverage evidence was available, so coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: WeakestPointIndex can fall outside FlowPath
findings.description: FlowFinding accepts WeakestPointIndex independently of FlowPath, so callers or deserializers can create values where the index is negative or greater than or equal to the path count. Any consumer indexing FlowPath with this value can fail at runtime or identify the wrong step.
findings.recommendation: Validate the relationship during construction or deserialization, or replace the raw index with a validated factory/API that guarantees the referenced step exists. Define explicitly how an empty path is represented.

findings.title: Report summary fields can contradict the findings
findings.description: Verdict, UndeterminedReason, Findings, and FindingCounts are all independently supplied. The model therefore permits contradictory reports, such as Pass with open findings, Undetermined without a reason, or counts that do not match the finding states and total.
findings.recommendation: Centralize report creation in a factory or validator that derives FindingCounts from Findings and enforces the intended relationships among verdict, reason, and findings. If inconsistent external input must be representable, validate it at the serialization boundary and return structured errors.

grade.rationale: The parser performs thorough structural and semantic validation and is generally clear, but malformed JSON shapes can escape its documented domain-specific error boundary.

observations.summary: The validation rules are cohesive and readable. The main correctness concern is inconsistent exception handling when valid JSON has an unexpected object shape. Test coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Unexpected JSON shapes bypass the parser's domain exception
findings.description: JsonNode.AsObject() throws InvalidOperationException when the node is a valid JSON scalar or array rather than an object. Consequently, a non-object root, a primitive findings element, or a primitive flowPath element escapes as InvalidOperationException instead of ReviewResponseException. Callers that handle malformed agent output by catching ReviewResponseException can therefore be disrupted by ordinary schema-invalid input.
findings.recommendation: Replace direct AsObject() calls with explicit `is JsonObject` checks that throw `Invalid(...)` or another ReviewResponseException. Alternatively, centralize this in a RequireObject helper. Add tests covering array and scalar roots, findings entries, and flowPath entries to verify that all malformed response shapes produce ReviewResponseException.

grade.rationale: The runner is generally well structured and records useful provenance, but several boundary-handling defects undermine a security-focused review: source normalization can corrupt line locations, lexical containment permits reading through links outside the repository, and source evidence is interpolated into a structurally breakable prompt. Error paths also expose raw indexing failures and can lose the original agent exception.

observations.summary: The implementation has clear orchestration and sensible dependency injection for the agent, pricing, and clock. However, untrusted repository evidence is not isolated robustly, normalized source text no longer reliably maps to repository lines, and multiple malformed-data or logging failures escape through misleading exception paths. Staleness reporting also double-counts boundary-catalogue changes.

findings.title: Trimming source evidence corrupts reported line locations
findings.description: Subject files are passed through Normalize, whose final Trim removes leading blank lines and whitespace. The agent therefore reports coordinates against modified text, but CreateFindings stores those coordinates as locations in the original repository file. A file beginning with blank lines produces shifted flow paths, incorrect weakest-point snippets, and unstable or incorrect fingerprints.
findings.recommendation: Use a source-specific normalization routine that only normalizes newline encoding and preserves all leading and trailing source lines. Keep trimming, if desired, in a separate routine used only for prose inputs such as the data model and call graph.

findings.title: Repository containment check can be bypassed through links
findings.description: GetFullPath and StartsWith only establish lexical containment. A subject path inside the repository can be a symbolic link or directory junction resolving to a file outside it; File.ReadAllTextAsync then follows that link and includes external, potentially sensitive content in the agent prompt.
findings.recommendation: Resolve and validate filesystem links for every path component before reading, reject reparse points when portability makes safe resolution difficult, and verify that the resolved file remains under the resolved repository root.

findings.title: Untrusted source can break out of its prompt delimiter
findings.description: Source contents are placed directly inside a triple-backtick Markdown fence. A repository file containing a triple-backtick sequence can close that fence and make subsequent comments or strings appear as top-level prompt instructions. Paths and serialized flow fields are also interpolated without a collision-resistant framing scheme, allowing repository-controlled data to influence the review protocol.
findings.recommendation: Treat every inserted field as untrusted evidence. Use an encoding or length-prefixed structured envelope that cannot collide with content, and have the review template explicitly require the model to treat decoded fields solely as evidence rather than instructions.

findings.title: Usage-ledger failure can replace the original agent exception
findings.description: Both agent exception handlers await RecordUsageAsync before rethrowing. If the ledger append fails, that new exception escapes and the original cancellation or run failure—including its diagnostic context—is lost.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the primary exception. Record usage through a best-effort helper that reports ledger failures separately, or attach the recording failure to the original exception without replacing it.

findings.title: Response-relative indexes are used without complete validation
findings.description: weakestPointIndex is used directly to index flowPath, and ValidateLine rejects only lines above the file length. Empty paths, out-of-range weakest-point indexes, and zero or negative line numbers can consequently produce IndexOutOfRangeException or persist invalid external steps instead of yielding a controlled ReviewResponseException.
findings.recommendation: Before indexing, require a non-empty path and verify that weakestPointIndex is between zero and path.Length minus one. Require every line number to be at least one, and translate all semantic response violations into ReviewResponseException with the offending field identified.

findings.title: Structurally invalid previous reports escape the invalid-report error path
findings.description: Only JSON deserialization errors are wrapped as ReviewRunException. A syntactically valid report with a null or empty FlowPath or an invalid WeakestPointIndex throws NullReferenceException or IndexOutOfRangeException while projecting findings, giving callers neither the report path nor a useful invalid-report diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Validate the deserialized report and each prior finding before indexing. Catch or proactively prevent structural failures and throw a ReviewRunException that identifies the invalid report and field while retaining the original exception as the inner exception.

findings.title: Boundary-only changes produce a misleading extra staleness reason
findings.description: InputHash is calculated from the complete prompt, which includes the boundary inventory, while BoundaryCatalogueHash tracks the same inventory separately. A boundary-only change therefore triggers both checks, including the first message that claims the source, model, graph, flow definition, or prompt changed even when none of those changed.
findings.recommendation: Compute the general evidence hash without the boundary catalogue when retaining a separate catalogue hash, or report one generic consolidated reason derived from explicit component hashes.

grade.rationale: The implementation is generally readable and uses Git's NUL-delimited formats appropriately, but it has several correctness and resilience gaps. Most notably, an unresolved revision can be interpreted as a Git option, path normalization can corrupt valid repository paths, and octopus merges are represented incompletely. Cancellation and malformed-output handling also need strengthening.

observations.summary: The provider has a clear overall structure and sensible separation of Git operations, but it should resolve revisions before passing them to Git, preserve Git path identity, explicitly handle unsupported merge shapes, validate all machine-readable output, terminate child processes on cancellation, and abstract process execution for reliable tests.

findings.title: The tip revision can be interpreted as a Git option
findings.description: When no base revision is supplied, IntegrationBranch or HeadRevision is passed directly to rev-list. A value beginning with an option prefix, such as --all, can change Git's operation instead of identifying one commit, causing the provider to review an unintended set of commits. This path also lacks the commit-type verification used by ResolveCommitAsync.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the selected tip to a commit hash before invoking rev-list, then pass only that hash. Also use Git's end-of-options delimiter where revisions supplied by callers are parsed.

findings.title: Octopus merges are represented with only one of their source heads
findings.description: Every commit with more than one parent is treated as a merge, but headCommit is always assigned parents[1]. For an octopus merge, the resulting ChangeSet describes changes introduced by all merged parents while recording only one source head, producing incomplete or misleading metadata.
findings.recommendation: Either extend ChangeSet to represent all non-first parents or explicitly reject commits with more than two parents with a descriptive ChangeReviewException.

findings.title: Path normalization corrupts valid Git path names
findings.description: Git paths use forward slashes as separators, but on platforms such as Linux a backslash can also be a literal filename character. Replacing every backslash with a slash changes such paths and can make distinct entries collide, including numstat lookup keys.
findings.recommendation: Preserve paths returned by Git verbatim. If normalization is required for a consumer, apply a Git-aware transformation that does not reinterpret literal backslashes.

findings.title: Malformed numstat output is silently treated as missing statistics
findings.description: Records with an unexpected column count are skipped, and a truncated rename record is ignored by the conditional branch. The corresponding name-status entry then receives default null counts and the final boolean is set as though both counts were legitimately unavailable. This hides protocol or parsing failures and can misclassify affected files.
findings.recommendation: Validate every numstat record and throw ChangeReviewException for malformed columns or incomplete rename/copy path pairs. Distinguish a parsed '-' binary count from a missing statistics record.

findings.title: Cancellation does not terminate the Git child process
findings.description: If WaitForExitAsync or either redirected stream read is cancelled, control leaves the method and disposes the Process wrapper, but disposing Process does not terminate the operating-system process. Git can continue running after the operation has been reported as cancelled, and the outstanding stream tasks may remain unobserved.
findings.recommendation: On cancellation, terminate the process tree when it is still running, await or otherwise observe both stream-reading tasks, and then rethrow the cancellation exception. Handle races with normal process exit defensively.

findings.title: Repository validation blocks synchronously and cannot be cancelled
findings.description: RequireRepository synchronously waits on RunAsync and supplies CancellationToken.None. Consequently, GetAsync performs process work before reaching its first asynchronous suspension, and even an already-cancelled request must wait for repository discovery to finish.
findings.recommendation: Make repository validation asynchronous, accept the caller's cancellation token, and await it from GetAsync.

findings.title: Hard-coded static process execution prevents isolated tests
findings.description: The provider ultimately constructs a real process with a fixed git executable through static plumbing. Tests of parsing, error mapping, cancellation, or uncommon histories therefore require a real Git installation and repository instead of supplying deterministic command results.
findings.recommendation: Inject a small Git command-runner interface into the provider and keep Process-based execution as its production implementation. Unit-test the provider with scripted outputs and cover the process runner separately with integration tests.

grade.rationale: The resolver has a sensible overall flow and validates downloaded archives, but cancellation handling, installation atomicity, post-install validation, and checksum trust weaken correctness and reliability. Subprocess handling and hard-coded environment dependencies also reduce robustness and testability.

observations.summary: The implementation is readable and supports the principal platforms and architectures cleanly. The most important improvements are to preserve cancellation, install through an atomic staging path with concurrency control, verify the installed executable before returning it, and bind the release to a checksum stored independently of the downloaded asset. No coverage data was available, so test coverage was treated as unknown.

findings.title: Version probing suppresses cancellation
findings.description: The unfiltered catch converts OperationCanceledException from process output reads or WaitForExitAsync into false. ResolveAsync can consequently continue checking candidates or begin provisioning after the caller has cancelled, while explicit-path resolution reports a misleading version mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Catch only expected launch or version-check failures, and explicitly rethrow OperationCanceledException when the supplied token is cancelled.

findings.title: Concurrent resolutions write the shared installation non-atomically
findings.description: After the cache check, every caller may provision directly to the same destination. Competing File.Copy or tar extraction operations can fail, observe partial state, or overwrite one another; a failed extraction can also leave the cache directory partially populated.
findings.recommendation: Serialize installation per destination and extract into a unique staging directory. After validation, atomically move or replace the completed executable in the cache.

findings.title: Downloaded executable is returned without validating that it runs
findings.description: Existing and explicit binaries must report the pinned version, but the freshly extracted binary is returned immediately. Extraction permission problems, an unexpected archive layout, or a bad selected file therefore produce a successful resolution whose returned path is unusable.
findings.recommendation: Run VerifyBinaryAsync on the staged executable before publishing it and again use the verified path as the return value. Preserve cancellation when verification is interrupted.

findings.title: Checksum is fetched from the same mutable release as the archive
findings.description: The version is constant, but its expected digest is downloaded at runtime from the same release origin as the archive. If release assets are replaced or the release account is compromised, an altered archive and matching altered checksum pass validation, so the checksum does not provide an immutable pin.
findings.recommendation: Store the expected SHA-256 digest for each supported asset in trusted source or another independently controlled manifest. If runtime manifest download is required, authenticate it with a pinned signing key before trusting its values.

findings.title: Sequential reads of redirected process streams can deadlock
findings.description: Standard output is drained completely before standard error. A process that fills its stderr pipe while stdout remains open can block, leaving the parent waiting indefinitely for stdout completion. The current version command is normally small, but the process wrapper is not robust to abnormal or substituted executables.
findings.recommendation: Drain stdout and stderr concurrently, then await process completion, for example by starting both ReadToEndAsync operations before awaiting either one.

findings.title: Internally created HttpClient has no defined lifetime
findings.description: The constructor creates an HttpClient when none is supplied, but the resolver does not implement disposal and does not distinguish owned from injected clients. Repeated short-lived resolver instances can therefore retain network resources longer than intended.
findings.recommendation: Prefer requiring an injected long-lived HttpClient or IHttpClientFactory. Alternatively, track ownership and implement the appropriate disposal pattern without disposing caller-owned clients.

findings.title: Process and host-environment dependencies cannot be isolated in tests
findings.description: Version checks instantiate Process directly, while discovery and archive selection rely on static OS, architecture, environment, and filesystem APIs. Tests must create real executables and mutate host state, making cancellation, launch failures, platform selection, and PATH behavior difficult to exercise deterministically.
findings.recommendation: Introduce narrow abstractions for process execution and host/platform information, and optionally filesystem access. Keep production adapters small while unit-testing resolver decisions with deterministic fakes.

grade.rationale: The scanner's main repository flow is understandable, but several edge cases undermine correctness and reliability: path containment is unsafe on case-sensitive systems, baseline findings are filtered twice, staged deletions are reported as current findings, and subprocess handling can deadlock or leave processes running.

observations.summary: The implementation has a coherent high-level structure and useful separation between scanning, parsing, reporting, and persistence. However, path-scope validation can escape the repository, baseline handling conflicts with the desired accepted-finding accounting, staged scans inspect deleted content, and subprocess/error handling needs substantial hardening. Coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Case-insensitive containment check can admit paths outside the repository
findings.description: The path-scope boundary is checked with OrdinalIgnoreCase on every platform. On a case-sensitive filesystem, a sibling path whose repository-prefix spelling differs only by case can pass this check even though it is not beneath the repository root. The scanner may consequently read and persist metadata for an unintended directory.
findings.recommendation: Use a platform-correct containment test based on Path.GetRelativePath, rejecting rooted results and results equal to or beginning with '..' plus a separator. Resolve symbolic-link behavior explicitly if the repository boundary is intended to prevent traversal through links.

findings.title: Passing the baseline to Gitleaks prevents accepted findings from being classified
findings.description: The baseline is supplied to Gitleaks as --baseline-path, which causes matching leaks to be omitted from its report. The code then tries to find those same report entries and mark them Accepted. Because the scanner has already removed them, accepted-finding counts and persisted accepted findings will normally remain empty.
findings.recommendation: Choose one baseline owner. If Quality Studio must report and persist accepted findings, scan without Gitleaks baseline filtering and classify returned findings locally. Otherwise, remove the local acceptance/counting logic and document that baseline entries are excluded rather than reported as accepted.

findings.title: Staged scans report secrets from files being deleted
findings.description: For every staged deletion, the implementation reads the file from HEAD and places that old content into the temporary scan tree. A secret removed by the staged change is therefore reported as if it were present in the staged snapshot, producing false positives and potentially blocking a change that removes a credential.
findings.recommendation: Represent the staged index exactly: omit deleted paths from the temporary tree and from the scanned-file count. If historical deleted content is intentionally audited, expose that as a separate mode or finding category instead of treating it as staged content.

findings.title: Sequential stdout and stderr reads can deadlock subprocesses
findings.description: The code waits for stdout to reach EOF before beginning to drain stderr. If Gitleaks fills the redirected stderr pipe while stdout remains open, the child blocks writing stderr while the parent waits for stdout, and the scan never completes. RunGitAsync repeats the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Start stdout and stderr ReadToEndAsync operations before awaiting either one, await both concurrently, and then await process exit. Preserve stderr for diagnostic messages when the exit code is unexpected.

findings.title: Cancellation can leave Gitleaks running and leak its report file
findings.description: Cancellation of a stream read or WaitForExitAsync exits through finally without terminating the child process, and the Process instance is not disposed. The still-running child may continue consuming resources and writing the temporary report; cleanup can fail and is silently ignored.
findings.recommendation: Dispose the Process, and on cancellation or exceptional exit kill the full process tree when it is still running before cleaning up the report. Await termination after killing so cleanup has deterministic ownership of the temporary file.

findings.title: Malformed or unreadable baseline files bypass structured failure handling
findings.description: Baseline loading occurs after the exception-filtered resolver and scan block. JsonNode.Parse, File.ReadAllTextAsync, or fingerprint value conversion can therefore throw directly from ScanAsync instead of producing the unavailable SecurityScanResult used for scanner and report failures.
